title: the issuer analyst on AMZN

notes.text: Operating cash flow generally exceeds net income across the last eight quarters, with the gap widening sharply in the latest quarter, so cash is supporting earnings rather than lagging them. The accruals ratio stays negative in most quarters and ends slightly positive, which points to some volatility rather than a clean deterioration trend.

Accounts receivable rises from $50.11B [f_74650949e536@2024-06-30] to $75.53B [f_74650949e536@2026-03-31] over the eight quarters, while revenue moves from $148B [f_14ad5dbd6560@2024-06-30] to $182B [f_14ad5dbd6560@2026-03-31]; receivables are growing faster than revenue. Inventory is more mixed: it rises to $41.49B [f_9ffebb96bd32@2025-09-30] and then eases to $36.53B [f_9ffebb96bd32@2026-03-31], while revenue rises from $148B [f_14ad5dbd6560@2024-06-30] to $182B [f_14ad5dbd6560@2026-03-31], so inventory is not growing faster than revenue over the full window.

On the quality read, the position looks worth keeping an eye on but not obviously larger on this evidence alone: receivables are building faster than sales, while cash from operations remains above net income. If anything, this supports a monitoring bias rather than an automatic size-up or cut.
